landing_faqA1: As long as it takes to create an account, then a few seconds per opportunity. From the first row, the follow-up countdown is running.
landing_faqA2: Your opportunities stay yours. They are never sold, nor used to train anything. Without an account, they never even leave your browser.
landing_faqA3: Each stage carries a delay. When the last contact date passes it, the opportunity enters your list for the day and goes into the 08:00 email. You reply, the counter restarts.
landing_faqA4: That is the idea. A spreadsheet waits for you; ProspectTracker comes to you: it surfaces what has gone quiet and lets you act instead of updating cells.
landing_faqA5: Yes. Columns and stages can be renamed, so an apprenticeship or job search tracks just as well. The default vocabulary is simply that of freelance contracting.
landing_faqQ1: How long does it take to get going?
landing_faqQ5: Does it work for anything other than freelancing?
landing_finalBody: Create your account by email or with Google, add your first opportunities — seconds each — and let follow-ups track the last contact date.

landing_remindersBody1: Yes, by email, without thinking about it. The delay is set stage by stage: three days after a CV is sent, seven after a first contact, fifteen if the recruiter told you to call back later.
landing_remindersBody2: The stages are yours. The five defaults — Saved, Contacted, CV Sent, Interview, Offer — can be renamed and recolored in two clicks.
